source.title: Optogenetic stimulation of a cortical biohybrid implant guides goal directed behavior

material: SU-8 microwell scaffold on fused silica bonded to glass coverslip (biohybrid implant)

formulation.evidence: 0.1 mg/mL Laminin (Millipore Sigma, L2020) in DI water

processing.evidence: SU-8 2010 photoresist (Kayaku) was spun at 3000 rpm
soft-baked at 95℃ for 3.5 minutes on a hotplate

post
exposure bake of 4 minutes at 95 ℃
ramping to 200℃ for 2 minutes on a hotplate
cured in an oven at 65℃ for 2 hours
centrifuged at 300 RCF for 5 minutes at room temperature

description.value: no visible sign of structural deterioration of the microwell scaffold
description.evidence:
no visible sign of
structural deterioration of the microwell scaffold even months after implantation

stability.conditions: in vivo, implanted on mouse cortex

other_outcomes.evidence: determined that on average we filled 77±15% (mean ± s.d., n=23 microwell scaffolds
other_outcomes.name: microwell loading fraction (24 h after loading)

other_outcomes.evidence:
we found 52±23% (mean±s.d.) of microwells to be
loaded with neurons expressing fluorescent protein
other_outcomes.name: microwells with fluorescent engrafted neurons three weeks after surgery

other_outcomes.evidence:
Five of nine mice in this
cohort passed criterion performance
other_outcomes.name: biohybrid mice reaching criterion performance

other_outcomes.evidence:
best session performance for biohybrid rate averaged 0.25±0.24 bits
per second
other_outcomes.name: best session bit rate (biohybrid)

notes: Microwells: 10 µm diameter, 15 µm deep, 15 µm pitch hexagonal lattice; implanted on cortical surface after craniectomy and duratomy. Neurons transduced with AAV CheRiff-eGFP or jRGECO1a.
